Mr. P.S. Kshirsagar, Advocate for the Petitioners.
Ms. Tajwar Khan, Agp for Respondent Nos.1, 3, 4, 5 & 6.
Mr. A.A. Kathane, Advocate for Respondent No.2.
Mr. C.R. Sharma, Advocate for Respondent No.7.
Coram : Nitin W. Sambre And M. M. Nerlikar, Jj.
Date : 8th July, 2025.

P.C. 
 The petitioner Sadanand Tikar and respondent No.7
 are the real brothers.

It appears that the petitioner has expired
 during the pendency of the petition and, as such, Sadanand's
 legal heirs are pursuing this petition.

2.  Amongst others, the reliefs claimed in the petition  are for issuance of directions to the respondent No.1/State  Government and respondent No.3 - Collector, Buldhana to  direct an enquiry against the respondent No.4 - Sub-Divisional  Officer, Khamgaon, who according to the petitioner, has  tampered with the official record and unauthorizedly released  the compensation in favour of respondent No.7 contrary to the  provisions of Section 3(H)(4) of the National Highways Act,
 1956.

1  3.
It appears that the land in question was acquired  pursuant to award dated 31st August, 2017 in which the  respondent No.4 has acted as a Land Acquisition Officer.

4. It appears that the original petitioner Sadanand  Tikar initially gave no objection for releasing compensation in  favour of respondent No.7, which was submitted before the  Tahsildar on 2nd May, 2016.
However, he raised an objection in  the acquisition proceedings for release of compensation on  19th December, 2017 with the respondent No.4 - Land  Acquisition Officer.

According to him, the respondent No.4 has  tampered with the documents while calling the report from the  Superintendent of Land Records, Khamgaon and changed the  date from 25th July, 2018 to 05th July, 2018.

According to him,
 the outward register was also tampered and outward  No.2685-A was subsequently inserted for the date 10th July,
 2018.

He would further claim that the actual entry in the  worksheet in regard to the aforesaid communication dated  25th /5th July, 2018 would be inferred from the outward register  which is at Annexure-12 and that being so he would claim that  the respondent No.4 has acted in high-handedness, arbitrarily  and mala fide manner while releasing the compensation in  favour of respondent No.7.
 5.

The counsel for respondent No.7 has strenuously  opposed the prayer on the ground that the petitioner has  already given up his claim vide undertaking dated 2nd May,
 2016 through a no objection certificate submitted before the  Tahsildar, Khamgaon, which claimed to be part of the  acquisition proceedings subsequently.
 907.WP.7155.2018.odt 3/4  6.
We fail to understand that

when an objection was  lodged by the petitioner with the respondent No.4 on  19th December, 2017 then what prompted him to release the  amount of acquisition in favour of respondent No.7 instead of  referring the matter to the Civil Court pursuant to the statutory  mandate provided under Section 3(H)(4) of the National  Highways Act.

Apart from above, perusal of the record depicts  shocking conduct on the part of the respondent No.4 as not  only the documents are incomplete in relation to processing the  request of respondent No.7 about release of amount but also  the tampering of record as has been claimed by the petitioner  as discussed hereinabove, can be prima facie inferred.
 7.
None of the Public Authorities have chosen to file  reply in the matter.

In that view of the matter, we deem it appropriate  to pass the following order:
 ORDER (i) We direct the Collector, Buldhana to take the entire record, in relation to the release of compensation processed by the respondent No.4, in his custody forthwith.
(ii) We further direct the Assistant Government Pleader Ms. Tajwar Khan to communicate this order telephonically to the Collector, Buldhana.

(iii) We further direct the Collector, Buldhana to retain photocopy of the entire record with him and shall ensure that the entire record is made available for perusal of this Court on 10th July, 2025.

(iv) We further direct the Collector, Buldhana to depute an Officer not below the rank of Additional Collector to file an affidavit in the matter and it shall be ensured that the Office of the Government Pleader shall receive the entire instructions in the matter before 10th July, 2025.

(v) We have passed the aforesaid order having regard to the fact that for almost more than six years neither the Collector nor the Sub-Divisional Officer, Khamgaon nor any of the Public Authorities have chosen to file reply in the matter.

9. Stand over to 10th July, 2025.
10.
Authenticated copy of this order be provided to the Assistant Government Pleader Ms. Tajwar Khan.
(M. M. NERLIKAR, J.) (NITIN W. SAMBRE, J.)
